samples.summary: No test for a CLI callback whose state token is expired/unknown — the branch whose old test this diff deleted
samples.evidence: The controller previously had an explicit branch: "State token was provided but invalid/expired — ... throw new BadRequestException('CLI login state expired or invalid...')", and the spec had a test exercising a non-CLI/unknown state token (`falls back to web flow when state token is not CLI`, removed by this diff). The new code path (auth.controller.ts:129-137) computes `cliState = consumeState(stateToken)`, and when that returns `undefined` (expired or unknown token) silently treats the callback as the **web** flow, checking `wafflebase_oauth_state` and clearing only that cookie — leaving the CLI cookie in place. No test in auth.controller.spec.ts covers a state token that is present but unknown/expired: grep for `expired`/`consumeState` in the spec returns nothing, and every CLI-flow test seeds a live state via `cliAuthStore.createState`. The behavior that replaced a deleted test now ships untested.

samples.summary: Callback never tested under NODE_ENV=production, so the `__Host-` state cookie name it must read is unverified on the read side
samples.evidence: cookies.ts computes the state cookie name per request: `secureCookies() ? '__Host-' + base : base`. github-auth.guard.spec.ts:155-180 pins the production (`__Host-`) name on the *write* side, but auth.controller.spec.ts only ever runs under the default NODE_ENV, so every callback test seeds the un-prefixed `wafflebase_oauth_state` / `wafflebase_cli_oauth_state` cookie. Nothing asserts that `consumeOAuthState` reads (and clears) the `__Host-`-prefixed name in production — a name mismatch between guard and controller in prod would break or bypass the binding and every existing test would still pass. The `describe('cookie SameSite policy')` block does flip NODE_ENV, but only exercises `logout`.

samples.summary: The `--allow-unbound-callback` commander option → `allowUnboundCallback` wiring (and its warning) is never parsed in any test
samples.evidence: login.test.ts:359-369 calls `runLogin({ allowUnboundCallback: true }, deps)` directly, i.e. it asserts the option object reaches the listener but never that commander's `--allow-unbound-callback` flag produces that option. Nothing anywhere parses the flag: grep for `allow-unbound-callback` across packages/cli finds only login.ts, README.md, schema/registry.ts and the string literals inside login.test.ts. The security-relevant downgrade flag's name-to-option mapping, the stderr warning at login.ts:227-231, and the `registerLoginCommand` catch/`process.exit(exitCode)` path (login.ts:78-86) are all untested; `classifyLoginFailure` is tested only as a pure function.

samples.summary: Two new error branches of the image gate have no test: the malformed-URL refusal and the INVALID_PROXY system error
samples.evidence: `assertFetchableImageUrl` blocks an unparseable `target` with 'Refusing to fetch malformed image URL' (and relies on `redactUrl` to strip userinfo from it), and `makeProxyAgent` raises `SystemError('INVALID_PROXY', ...)` when the configured proxy URI is unusable. Grepping image-fetcher.test.ts for `malformed`, `INVALID_PROXY`, `redactUrl` returns no matches — the only hit is an unrelated 'opaque-filters' test. Both branches are new code with no coverage; the malformed case is also the one where credential redaction of an unparseable URL is claimed but not asserted.

samples.summary: Test named "without writing the file" asserts only the exit code, never that no file was written
samples.evidence: `it('exits 2 on a 401 without writing the file', ...)` sets the stub response, runs `docs export doc-1 out.pdf`, and asserts only `expect(process.exitCode).toBe(2)`. There is no spy on `writeFileSync`/`writeBinary` and no filesystem assertion, so the 'without writing the file' half of the claim is unverified — the test would pass if the command wrote out.pdf.

samples.summary: New schema-registry parameter entry for `--allow-unbound-callback` is not asserted by schema.test.ts
samples.evidence: registry.ts adds `'--allow-unbound-callback'` under the `login` command's parameters. schema.test.ts asserts registry contents for docs.list/docs.create flags and safety levels, but has no assertion on `login`'s parameters and no generic cross-check that registry parameters match the commander options actually registered, so the new entry (and any future drift from the real flag) is uncovered.

finding.summary: The guard→strategy state hand-off (`req.__oauthState` → `opts.state`) is renamed in this diff and has no test at all
finding.evidence: `github.strategy.ts` was changed from reading `__cliStateToken` to `__oauthState` and forwarding it as `opts.state` — the single wire that actually gets the CSRF-binding `state` to GitHub (the guard's own comment says "a typo in it would silently drop the binding"). `github.strategy.spec.ts` only asserts endpoint URLs (lines 33-119); it never constructs a request with `__oauthState` and never observes what is passed to `super.authenticate`. `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` asserts only that the guard *sets* `req.__oauthState`; nothing on either side proves the two names agree or that the state is forwarded. A mismatch would leave every web login unbound-or-broken with a fully green suite.

searchedFor: grep for other backend specs referencing wafflebase_oauth_state
finding.summary: The web-state comparison is only tested with different-length values, so the actual constant-time comparison branch is never exercised
finding.evidence: `timingSafeEqualString` short-circuits on `left.length === right.length` before calling `timingSafeEqual`. The mismatch fixtures are `'mine'` (4 chars) vs `'theirs'` (6 chars) and `{}` vs `'theirs'` — every rejecting case is decided by the length check alone. The real attack shape is an attacker-supplied `state` of the *same* length as the victim's cookie (both are 43-char base64url values from `randomBytes(32)`), and no test covers it: an implementation that returned `true` for equal-length differing values would still pass this suite.
